title: Bassoon with the state band, the symphony and Ralph Font's hotel orchestra
summary: He joined the Puerto Rican National Band at two hundred dollars a month, then the symphony and Ralph Font at the Americana, doubling on piccolo, oboe and bassoon.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: How did work turn out for you there?

Well, I went to Puerto Rico -- I called a friend of mine from New York and asked him what the situation was down there and he said, 'Well, in the national band -- the state band, they'd like to have a bassoon player.' I said, 'Okay, I'm coming down.' So, we arrived in Puerto Rico on a

Sunday night and by Tuesday night I was working with the National Orchestra -- National Band, playing bassoon. They didn't have a decent bassoon player on the Island at that time. But the gimmick was, it only paid $200.00 a month. Mind you, $200.00 a month. But we had some aid. I stayed with my sister-in-law and her husband is one of the important horse trainers there and they had a big house, so they kept the four of us until I got on my feet. So I just turned over my -- when it got to me it was $190.00 a month and I just turned it over to my sister and gave her $130.00 a month and she fed us and took care until I got a break. Finally, I went from there to -- from the State Band -- I left and I joined the Puerto Rican Symphony. Oh, there was an increase of salary, about $116.00 a week -- a week. Oh, I was rich then. And I stayed with the symphony a season and a half and one day I was in a cleaning establishment and I met one of the conductors at one of the hotels, and he asked me if I'd like to join him. He heard that I was in town. I said, 'Yeah, I'd be glad to.' So, he gave me a job at the Americano with Ralph Font's orchestra and that was an increase to about $140.00 or something like that. And I stayed a couple years at the Americana and I left there and went to the San Juan Hotel -- they needed a piccolo player. When I arrived in Puerto Rico there weren't many guys who could double.
